answer: Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 17 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. Histories are stored in timber, checked in marble, and kernel makes public each void. A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 2 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
